seo.title: EduBeam: free structural analysis online
seo.description: Free 2D structural analysis in your browser. Draw beams, frames and trusses, add loads and get N, V, M diagrams, reactions and deflections instantly.

hero.title: Structural analysis online.
hero.lede: EduBeam is a free structural analysis app for beams, frames and trusses. Draw a model in your browser and its diagrams, reactions and deflections update with every edit.
hero.note: Free and open source. No install, no account.

heritage.title: Open source, with roots in the classroom
heritage.body: EduBeam carries on the desktop EduBeam, created at the Department of Mechanics of the Faculty of Civil Engineering, CTU in Prague, and it still opens that program’s session files. The web edition is free and open source, and so is {'@'}edubeam/fem, the solver behind every number on this page.

simple.name: Simply supported beam
simple.hint: Take moments about A to find the reaction at B, then sum the vertical forces for A. The largest moment is where the shear force crosses zero, or under a point load.

cantilever.name: Cantilever
cantilever.hint: Every reaction is at the wall: sum the vertical forces, then take moments about A. A cantilever’s largest moment is at the wall.

overhang.name: Beam with an overhang
overhang.hint: Take moments about A for the reaction at B. Then compare two candidates for the largest moment: in the span, where V = 0, and over B, where the overhang hogs.

gerber.name: Gerber beam
gerber.hint: Start with GC: it rests on the hinge G and the roller C, and a hinge carries no moment. Then load ABG with the force the hinge passes on, and solve it as a beam with an overhang.

threeHinged.name: Three-hinged frame
threeHinged.hint: Moments about A and about E give the vertical reactions. Then cut at the crown hinge C, where M = 0, and take moments about C for one half: that gives the horizontal thrust.

truss.name: Warren truss
truss.hint: Find the reactions from the whole truss. Then cut through three bars, one of them the bar you want, and take moments about the joint where the other two meet; for a diagonal, sum the vertical forces instead.

continuous.name: Two-span continuous beam
continuous.hint: One redundant: take the moment over B as the unknown. The three-moment equation, with M = 0 at A and C, gives it directly; the reactions then follow span by span.

portal.name: Portal frame
portal.hint: One redundant: release the horizontal reaction at D, find the horizontal movement of D under the loads and under a unit force there (virtual work, with M diagrams), and make it zero.

seo.description: A finite element solver for plane beams, frames and trusses in TypeScript: hinges, temperature and settlement loads, load cases, exact internal forces.

analyses.title: Analyses
analyses.body: Linear statics with as many load cases as you need. Diagrams are exact between the nodes: no mesh to refine.

elements.title: Elements
elements.body: A two-node Timoshenko beam in the x–z plane. Hinged at both ends it is a truss bar.

loads.title: Loads
loads.body: Nodal forces and moments, point, uniform and trapezoidal loads along members, temperature, settlements.

results.title: Results
results.body: N, V and M anywhere along a member, deflected shapes, end forces, displacements and reactions.

behind.title: The solver behind EduBeam
behind.body: Every diagram, reaction and deflection in EduBeam, and every figure on this site, is computed by {name}.

plot.tagline: Vue components that draw plane structures and their results, in the figures’ own style.

seo.title: {'@'}edubeam/plot: structural diagrams for Vue
seo.description: Vue components that draw plane structures, loads, reactions and N, V, M diagrams as a textbook does, for course pages, slides, exercises and SVG files.

try.title: Try it
try.lede: A frame solved by {'@'}edubeam/fem on this page. Change what is drawn; the code follows.

teaching.title: Made for teaching material
teaching.lede: A model in code is a figure that can't go out of date: change a number and the drawing, the reactions and the diagrams follow. A seed picks a new exercise; the same seed always gives the same one. This site's {practice} and {exam} are made this way.

exercises.title: Exercises and tests
exercises.body: One exercise per student from a seed, with its answer key, printed or as figures for LaTeX and Word.

slides.title: Slides and notes
slides.body: Figures that build up click by click in Slidev, Vue or Beamer, solved live.

embedding.title: In your docs and apps
embedding.body: Vite, VitePress or Nuxt, rendered on the server, or from pre-solved JSON.

print.title: Files for print
print.body: A standalone SVG with plain colours, for Word, LaTeX and Inkscape.

style.title: In the figures’ style
style.body: Members, supports, loads, reactions and hatched diagrams as on this site, with chain dimensions and named unknown reactions for exercise sheets.

readable.title: Readable at any size
readable.body: Text and lines keep their pixel size; values that would collide are moved or dropped, never clipped.

exact.title: Exact
exact.body: Diagrams are the solver’s own polynomials: extremes found exactly, steps at point loads drawn as steps.

fits.title: Fits a page
fits.body: Colours from your CSS, light and dark. Renders on the server and never captures scrolling.

seo.ogTitle: Statics practice problems with instant answers
seo.ogDescription: Beams, frames and trusses with fresh numbers every time. Check your reactions and moments instantly, then see the diagrams.

practice.title: Practice statics
practice.lede: A new problem every time, with its exact answers to check yours against. Work it out on paper, type in what you get, and then see the diagrams.
practice.codes: Every problem has a code, such as {code}. The same code is always the same problem: share it with a classmate, or open the one your teacher gave you.

structures.title: Structures
structures.legend: Structures that New problem picks from
structures.note: New problem picks one of these at random.

code.label: Problem code
code.error: That is not a problem code. A code is a letter and a number, such as H2048.

answers.title: Your answers
answers.note: The reactions are drawn on the problem the way they count as positive. If one acts the other way, its answer is negative.

verdict.allRight: All correct. The diagrams are now drawn on the problem.
verdict.sign: {right} of {total} right. Where it says {sign}, the size is right and the direction is not.
verdict.revealed: The exact answers are beside your fields, and the diagrams are drawn on the problem.

practice.solved: Solved on this device: {n} problem. | Solved on this device: {n} problems.

answers.title: Where the answers come from
answers.body: Each problem is solved in your browser by {solver}, the solver behind EduBeam, and drawn by {plot}. The largest moment is found exactly, not read off a sampled curve.

signs.title: Signs and units
signs.body: Answers are in kN and kNm. Loads act downwards unless the problem says otherwise. Reactions are positive to the right, upwards and counter-clockwise, as each field shows; bar forces are positive in tension. The diagrams follow EduBeam’s {conventions}.

teachers.title: For teachers
teachers.body: The {exam} prints these problems as test papers, a different version for each student, with an answer key. Each problem’s code lets students check their own answers here afterwards.
